transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep getting up when I’m supposed to stay seated. It happens during client interviews, tutoring sessions, even book club. I’ll be trying to sit and listen, and I just… get up. People are starting to notice, and it’s becoming a problem.
When you’re sitting and then get up, do you feel an inner sense of restlessness?

Yes. It’s like I can’t really shut off. Even on days when I’m not out doing field work, I’m still moving around—unpacking boxes, reorganizing case files, running errands—like I’m still chasing a lead. I have a hard time just being off duty and sitting still.
Did this restless need to get up start after you began taking a medication or after a dose was increased?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed it starting right after a medication change or anything like that. It feels more like it’s just been there, but I can’t really tie it to a dose increase.
Were you already this restless as a child?

Yes, I was. My grade-school report cards pretty much always said I was bright, but couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks or conversations?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s my attention specifically that’s the problem in conversations or tasks. I’d have to think about it more.
Do you often have trouble keeping your attention on what someone is saying to you?
I’m not sure. I mean, I hear people, but I haven’t really tracked whether I’m losing attention to what they’re saying specifically. I’d need to think about that more.
Have you had times when your mood was unusually high or irritable?
I’m not sure I’d call it unusually high. Irritable, maybe at times, but I haven’t really noticed clear episodes where my mood is way above normal or anything like that.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really paid attention to whether waiting my turn is a problem for me. I’d have to think about that a bit.
Do you often get easily distracted when you’re trying to focus on something?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can get sidetracked sometimes, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it happens a lot when I’m trying to focus.
Do you often have difficulty organizing tasks and activities?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do have a lot of moving parts in my work, so I use notes and lists, but I haven’t really thought about whether organizing tasks is a consistent problem for me.
Do you often fidget with your hands or feet, or squirm in your seat?

Yes, I do. Especially when I’m stuck at the computer going through records. My foot will be bouncing under the desk, or I’ll be clicking a pen, shifting around in the chair… sometimes enough that I lose my place in what I’m reading.
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve never had voices like that when no one was there.
When you feel like you have to get up, do you also feel anxious?

Not really anxious, no. It’s more like I just can’t stay put. I’ll be in a client interview, or tutoring, or even book club, and I keep needing to get up when I’m supposed to be sitting and listening. People have started noticing, which is part of why I brought it up.
Do you ever feel an urge to pull out your hair?
No, I haven’t noticed any urge to pull out my hair.
Have you had times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy the next day?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep great, but I wouldn’t say I felt full of energy the next day. Usually I feel it if I don’t sleep enough.
When you get up, does moving around make that restless feeling feel better?

A little, yeah. It’s not like it fixes everything, but getting up and moving around feels better than trying to force myself to sit still. The problem is it happens when I’m supposed to stay put, like in client interviews or tutoring or book club, and people are starting to notice.
Do you also feel this restless need to move when you’re standing?

Yeah, I think so. Even when I’m already standing, I don’t really stay still. If I’m not out in the field, I’ll bounce from unpacking boxes to reorganizing case files to running errands, like I’m still chasing something. I have a hard time just being off duty.

Are you currently taking, or have you recently taken, any antipsychotic or anti-nausea medication such as aripiprazole, risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, haloperidol, metoclopramide, or prochlorperazine?
Not that I know of. I don’t think I’m taking any of those, and I haven’t recently, as far as I can remember.
